body.text: sāndrodrekakṣubhitam abhitaḥ svāntam antar niyamya prāyo dhatte navanavarasollekham ānandakandam // 1
body.translated_text: Having restrained within the mind that is agitated all around with intense and surging [emotions], it mostly bears an ever-new delineation of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic experience), the source of bliss.

body.text: bhūyo bhūyaḥ pralayavibhavoddāmaduḥkhāntarāyo yo 'sāv antar jayati hṛdaye ko 'pi saṃvidvikāsaḥ // 2
body.translated_text: That certain ineffable expansion of consciousness which triumphs within the heart, again and again — its obstacles being the fierce sufferings born of the power of dissolution.

body.text: iha khalu nikhilajagadātmā sarvottīrṇaś ca sarvamayaś ca vikalpāsaṃkucitasaṃvitprakāśarūpaḥ anavacchinnacidānandaviśrāntaḥ prasaradaviralavicitrapañcavāhavāhavāhinīmahodadhiḥ niratiśayasvātantryasīmani pragalbhamānaḥ sarvaśaktikhacita eka eva asti saṃvid ātmā maheśvaraḥ // 3
body.translated_text: Here indeed, the Self of the entire universe, both utterly transcendent and all-encompassing, whose nature is the light of consciousness uncontracted by thought-constructs, who rests in unlimited <s>cit</s> (consciousness) and <s>ānanda</s> (bliss), who is the great ocean of the streaming, copious, and diverse army of the five flows, who boldly stands at the frontier of supreme autonomy, inlaid with all powers — He alone exists: <s>Saṃvid</s> (Consciousness), the Self, <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord).

body.text: tasya prakāśarūpatā cicchaktiḥ svātantryam ānandaśaktiḥ taccamatkāraḥ icchāśaktiḥ āmarśātmakatā jñānaśaktiḥ sarvākārayogitvaṃ kriyāśaktiḥ iti // 4
body.translated_text: His nature as luminosity is <s>cicchakti</s> (power of consciousness); His autonomy is <s>ānandaśakti</s> (power of bliss); His wonder is <s>icchāśakti</s> (power of will); His nature as reflective awareness is <s>jñānaśakti</s> (power of knowledge); His union with all forms is <s>kriyāśakti</s> (power of action).

body.text: itthaṃ sarvaśaktiyoge 'pi ābhir mukhyābhiḥ śaktibhir upacaryate sa ca bhagavān svātantryaśaktimahimnā svātmānaṃ saṃkucitam iva ābhāsayan aṇuḥ iti ucyate // 5
body.translated_text: Thus, although possessing all powers, He is designated by these principal powers. And that Blessed Lord, by the greatness of His <s>svātantryaśakti</s> (power of autonomy), manifesting Himself as if contracted, is called <s>aṇu</s> (the atomic self).
As it has been said: "<s>Śiva</s> is indeed all-pervading, but through the seal of self-willed contraction,
due to the force of the flood of <s>karmas</s> of varied fruit, He assumes various bodies."

body.text: iti nijasvarūpagopanakelilolam evaṃ māheśaśaktiparispandaṃ pravaraguravaḥ pratipedire // 8
body.translated_text: Thus the supreme <s>gurus</s> (teachers) have understood this vibration (<s>parispanda</s>) of <s>Maheśa's</s> (the Great Lord's) power as playfully delighting in concealing its own true nature.

body.text: tathā ca āhuḥ atidurghaṭakāritvāt svācchandyanirmalād asau // 9
body.translated_text: And thus they have said: "Because of accomplishing what is supremely difficult, through His spotless freedom,
the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) is skilled in the play of concealing His own Self.
Even though His true nature is unobscured, the self-concealment of the All-Pervading Lord —

body.text: saivāvidyā yato bheda etāvān viśvavṛttikaḥ iti // 12
body.translated_text: that itself is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), from which arises this differentiation, extensive as the entire cosmic process."

body.text: na ca etāvatā bhagavato deśakālākāropādhivirahitaniratiśayānandaparisyandātmakasya kācid api kṣatiḥ pratyuta paramamahimnaḥ paripuṣṭir ity uktam // 13
body.translated_text: Nor is there any diminishment whatsoever of the Blessed Lord, whose essence is the overflowing of unsurpassed bliss devoid of the limiting conditions of space, time, and form; rather, it has been said to be the fullest nourishment of His supreme majesty.
"If the Great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>) were to remain with a body of one form alone,
He would have forfeited His <s>maheśvaratva</s> (great lordship) and <s>saṃvittva</s> (consciousness-nature), like a pot and such.
For limited luminosity is indeed the characteristic of inert matter (<s>jaḍa</s>).

body.text: jaḍād vilakṣaṇo bodho yato na parimīyate // 17
body.translated_text: Consciousness (<s>bodha</s>) is distinct from the inert precisely because it cannot be delimited.
Therefore, from the great ocean of consciousness, His own powers surge forth playfully,
taking refuge in the marvelous diversity of self-collision, like waves."
And so forth.

body.text: tad evam asau bhagavān svamāyāśaktyākhyena avyabhicaritasvātantryaśaktimahimnā svātmanaiva ātmānaṃ saṃkucitam iva avabhāsayan vijñānākalaḥ pralayākalaḥ sakalaś ca sampadyate // 21
body.translated_text: Thus that Blessed Lord, by the greatness of His unfailing <s>svātantryaśakti</s> (power of autonomy), known as His own <s>māyāśakti</s> (power of illusion), manifesting His own Self as if contracted through Himself alone, becomes <s>vijñānākala</s> (the knowledge-only being), <s>pralayākala</s> (the dissolution-only being), and <s>sakala</s> (the complete being).

body.text: tatra āṇavena ekenaiva malena saṃyukto vijñānākala ucyate dvābhyām āṇavamāyī yābhyām apavedyaḥ pralayākalaḥ tribhir āṇavamāyīyakārmaiḥ saṃvedyaḥ tair eva kalādidharaṇyantatattvamayaḥ sakalaḥ tadartham eva ayam arthasargaḥ // 22
body.translated_text: Among these, the one conjoined with the single <s>āṇava mala</s> (impurity of limitation) alone is called <s>vijñānākala</s>; the one beyond experience, conjoined with two — <s>āṇava</s> and <s>māyīya</s> [impurities] — is the <s>pralayākala</s>; the one who is an experiencer, conjoined with three — <s>āṇava</s>, <s>māyīya</s>, and <s>kārma</s> [impurities] — constituted of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles) from <s>kalā</s> down to <s>dharaṇī</s> (earth), is the <s>sakala</s>. For this purpose alone is this emanation of objects.

body.text: tatra sṛṣṭyunmukho bhagavān śuddhādhvani vartamānaḥ svaśaktibhiḥ māyāṃ vikṣobhya kalātattvaṃ kiṃcitkartṛtvalakṣaṇaṃ pudgalasya sṛjati tato 'pi kiṃcid avabodhākhyaṃ vidyātattvaṃ kiṃcid abhilāṣarūpaṃ ca rāgatattvaṃ tad etat sarāgaṃ kartṛtattvaṃ bhūtabhaviṣyadvartamānatayā tridhā avacchidyate tat kālatattvaṃ tulyatve 'pi rāge yena kartṛtvasya avacchedaḥ kriyate tat niyatitattvaṃ tad etat kañcukaṣaṭkam antarmalāvṛtasya pudgalasya bahir ācchādakam uktaṃ ca cillācakreśvaramate māyā kalā śuddhavidyā rāgakālau niyantraṇā // 23
body.translated_text: There, the Blessed Lord, facing toward creation and abiding in the pure path, agitating <s>Māyā</s> through His own powers, creates the <s>kalā tattva</s> (principle of limited agency) characterized by limited doership for the individual soul (<s>pudgala</s>); from that also He creates the <s>vidyā tattva</s> (principle of limited knowledge) known as partial awareness; and the <s>rāga tattva</s> (principle of attachment) in the form of longing. This agent-principle endowed with attachment is divided threefold as past, future, and present — that is the <s>kāla tattva</s> (principle of time). That by which doership is delimited even when attachment is equal — that is the <s>niyati tattva</s> (principle of necessity). These six coverings (<s>kañcukas</s>) are the outer covering of the individual soul whose inner impurity is veiled. As stated in the <s>Cillācakreśvaramata</s>: "<s>Māyā</s>, <s>kalā</s>, <s>śuddhavidyā</s>, <s>rāga</s>, <s>kāla</s>, and <s>niyati</s> —"
"these six, by the force of concealment, are the <s>kañcukas</s> (coverings) of the limited self."
"Thus the inner <s>mala</s> (impurity) of the individual soul (<s>pudgala</s>) remains like a covering,
the <s>kañcukas</s> (coverings) are like husks; therefore, he is devoid of [full] knowledge and action."
Thus [ends the quotation].

body.text: sā ca kalā puruṣasya parimitaṃ kartṛtvaṃ prakāśya sukhaduḥkhamoharūpaṃ bhogyam avyaktatvaṃ sṛjati tato 'pi aṣṭaguṇaṃ buddhitattvam utpannaṃ tato 'pi sāttvikarājasatāmasabhedabhinnaṃ triskandham ahaṃkāratattvam tatra pūrvasmāt ahaṃkārāt mano jātam aparasmāt indriyāṇi tṛtīyāt tanmātrāṇi ebhyo bhūtāni ity evam ayam ekasyaiva ādidevasya svātantryamahimnā saṃsāre saṃsarataḥ parimitapramātṛtām avalambamānasya tattvaprasaraḥ uktaṃ ca bhūtāni tanmātragaṇendriyāṇi mūlaṃ pumān kañcukayuk suśuddham // 28
body.translated_text: And that <s>kalā</s>, having manifested limited doership for <s>puruṣa</s> (the individual soul), creates <s>avyakta</s> (the unmanifest) as the object of experience in the form of pleasure, pain, and delusion. From that arises the <s>buddhi tattva</s> (principle of intellect) endowed with eight qualities; from that again, the <s>ahaṃkāra tattva</s> (principle of ego) divided into three groups by the distinctions of <s>sāttvika</s> (pure), <s>rājasa</s> (passionate), and <s>tāmasa</s> (dark). Among these, from the first <s>ahaṃkāra</s> arises <s>manas</s> (mind); from the second, the <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs); from the third, the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements); and from these, the <s>bhūtas</s> (gross elements). Thus this is the emanation of principles of the one Primordial God (<s>Ādideva</s>) alone, who by the greatness of His autonomy transmigrates in <s>saṃsāra</s> while assuming the state of a limited knower. As stated: "The <s>bhūtas</s>, <s>tanmātras</s>, groups of <s>indriyas</s>, the root [<s>prakṛti</s>], <s>puruṣa</s> conjoined with the coverings, and the perfectly pure —"
"up to <s>Vidyā</s> and ending with <s>Śakti</s> — such is the expansive display of waves spreading from the ocean of one's own consciousness."

body.text: tathā saala utta puriṣuṇṇa u saallutta uttiṇṇa // 30
body.translated_text: Likewise [in Apabhraṃśa]: "The <s>sakala</s> has arisen; the <s>puruṣa</s> is filled; and that which transcends the <s>sakala</s> has emerged.

body.text: pari āṇaha attāṇa u pari masiveṇa samāṇa u // 31
body.translated_text: The Self is known through <s>āṇava</s> (limitation); and it is equal with the supreme."
Thus [ends the quotation].

body.text: eteṣāṃ ca uktarūpāṇāṃ tattvānāṃ pramātṛbhede vaicitryāt prameyavaicitryaṃ bhavati iti śrīpūrvaśāstre kathitam tathā hi śaktimacchaktibhedena dharātattvaṃ vibhidyate // 33
body.translated_text: And for these principles of the forms described, because of the diversity of knowing subjects, there arises diversity of objects of knowledge — thus it is stated in the sacred <s>Pūrvaśāstra</s>: "By the distinction of empowered and powerless, the <s>dharā tattva</s> (earth principle) is divided.
Together with its own nature, it should be known as fifteenfold.
By this very arrangement, from the <s>puruṣa</s> principle up to <s>kalā</s>,
it should be known as thirteenfold; the <s>pralayākala</s> is like <s>Rudra</s>.
Likewise <s>Māyā</s> should be known as ninefold; the <s>jñānakevala</s> (knowledge-only being);
the <s>Mantras</s> are sevenfold; likewise the <s>Mantranāyakas</s> (Mantra-lords) are fivefold;

body.text: tridhā mantreśvareśānāḥ śivaḥ sākṣān na bhidyate // 39
body.translated_text: the <s>Mantreśvaras</s> (Mantra-lords) and <s>Īśānas</s> (Rulers) are threefold; <s>Śiva</s> directly is not divided.

body.text: yaḥ punaḥ sarvatattvāni vetty etāni yathārthataḥ // 40
body.translated_text: He who knows all these principles as they truly are —
he is declared to be a <s>guru</s> (teacher) equal to Me, a revealer of the power of <s>mantras</s>.

body.text: dṛṣṭāḥ sambhāṣitās tena spṛṣṭāś ca prīticetasā // 42
body.translated_text: Those seen, spoken to, and touched by him with a loving mind —
people are freed from sins committed even over seven births."
Thus [ends the quotation].
Thus this sequence of principles (<s>tattvakrama</s>) has multiple levels of determination.

body.text: eteṣāṃ ca tattvānāṃ vargaśo yad anugāmi rūpam ekarūpam ekarūpakalanāsahiṣṇutvāt sā kalā kathyate // 46
body.translated_text: And the uniform nature that follows these principles group by group, because of its capacity for unitary assimilation, is called <s>kalā</s> (phase of manifestation).

body.text: tathā hi nivartante yatas tattvavargāḥ sā nivṛttir nāma kalā // 47
body.translated_text: Thus, that from which the groups of principles cease is the <s>kalā</s> called <s>Nivṛtti</s> (cessation).
And it is established in the earth [principle] alone.

body.text: kāraṇatve pūraṇāpyāyakāritvāt pratiṣṭhā nāma kalā ucyate // 49
body.translated_text: Because of its nature of filling and nourishing in causation, it is called the <s>kalā</s> named <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s> (foundation).
And it pervades and is established from water up to <s>mūlaprakṛti</s> (primordial nature).
When the knowable dissolves, due to the predominance of consciousness, the <s>kalā</s> named <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge) [is so named].
And it presides over the path from <s>puruṣa</s> (soul) up to <s>Māyā</s>.
Because of the subsiding of the waves of the coverings (<s>kañcukas</s>), the <s>kalā</s> called <s>Śāntā</s> (peaceful) is so named.
And it is established from <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (pure knowledge) up to the end of <s>Śakti</s>.
This itself is the fourfold cosmic egg (<s>aṇḍacatuṣṭaya</s>), characterized as <s>pārthiva</s> (earthly), <s>prākṛta</s> (natural), <s>māyīya</s> (illusory), and <s>śākta</s> (pertaining to power).
Because of transcending all, in the <s>Śiva tattva</s> there is <s>Śāntyatītā</s> (that which transcends peace).
Thus.

body.text: paraṃ tu tattvaṃ svatantratvāt kalātītam āsām eva kalānāṃ tattvavad antarbhūtāni bhuvanāny api boddhavyāni evaṃ sthūlasūkṣmaparatvena bhuvanatattvakalārūpaṃ trividharūpaṃ prameyam uktam pramāṇam api tathaiva padamantravarṇatayā trividham eva iti ekasyaiva pūrṇapramātuḥ svātantryāt saṃsarataḥ ṣaḍvidhe adhvani viśrāntir uktā // 58
body.translated_text: But the supreme principle, being autonomous, transcends the <s>kalās</s>. The worlds (<s>bhuvanas</s>) should also be understood as included within these very <s>kalās</s>, just as the principles are. Thus, the objects of knowledge are described as threefold in the form of worlds, principles, and <s>kalās</s>, by way of gross, subtle, and supreme. Likewise, the means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is also threefold — as <s>pada</s> (word), <s>mantra</s>, and <s>varṇa</s> (phoneme). Thus the repose of the one perfect Knower who, by His autonomy, transmigrates in the sixfold path (<s>ṣaḍadhvan</s>) has been described.

body.text: bhavanti cātra dīkṣāparighaṭanasaṃgrahaślokāḥ padamantravarṇam ekaṃ puraṣoḍaśakaṃ dhareti ca nivṛttiḥ // 59
body.translated_text: And here are the summary verses for the arrangement of <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation): "<s>Nivṛtti</s> holds one <s>pada</s>, one <s>mantra</s>, one <s>varṇa</s>, and sixteen worlds.
The next [<s>Pratiṣṭhā</s>] has twenty-three principles, eleven <s>varṇas</s>, five worlds, five <s>mantras</s>, and [corresponding] <s>padas</s>.
The other <s>kalā</s> [<s>Vidyā</s>] has seven principles and <s>varṇas</s>, two <s>padas</s> and two <s>mantras</s>, and ten worlds.
The fourth [<s>Śāntā</s>] has three <s>varṇas</s> and three principles, one <s>pada</s>, one <s>mantra</s>, and four worlds.

body.text: ṣoḍaśa varṇāḥ padamantratattvam ekaṃ ca śāntyatīteyam // 63
body.translated_text: <s>Śāntyatītā</s> has sixteen <s>varṇas</s>, one <s>pada</s>, one <s>mantra</s>, and one principle."
Thus [ends the quotation].

body.text: tad evam āṇavīṃ vṛttim ālambya bhagavān vicitraiḥ jātyāyurbhogaiḥ jarāyujāṇḍajodbhedajasvedajādijātaṃ prādurbhāvayati // 65
body.translated_text: Thus, resorting to the <s>āṇavī vṛtti</s> (the mode of the limited self), the Blessed Lord brings forth beings born in diverse forms of birth, lifespan, and experience — born from the womb (<s>jarāyuja</s>), born from eggs (<s>aṇḍaja</s>), born by bursting forth (<s>udbhedaja</s>), and born from moisture (<s>svedaja</s>).

body.text: tatra upabhuktasya annapānasya pākavaśāt rasarūpatayā sthitasya raktamāṃsamedo'sthimajjātmanā śukradhātau viśrāntir bhavati tatra imāḥ prajāḥ prajāyante // 66
body.translated_text: There, food and drink that has been consumed, having undergone digestion and remaining in the form of vital essence (<s>rasa</s>), finds its final repose in the <s>śukra dhātu</s> (seminal element) through [the stages of] blood, flesh, fat, bone, and marrow. From that, these beings are born.

body.text: tathā coktaṃ sauśrute iha khalu pāñcabhautikasya caturvidhasya āhārasya ṣaḍrasopetasya dvividharasavīryasya aṣṭavidharasavīryasya anekaprakāropabhuktasya pariṇatasya yas tejorūpaḥ sāraḥ sūkṣmaḥ sa rasa ity ucyate tasya hṛdayaṃ sthānaṃ sa ca hṛdayāt caturviṃśatidhamanīr anupraviśya ūrdhvagā daśa daśa ca adhogāminīḥ catasraḥ tiryaggāḥ sakalaṃ śarīram aharahas tarpayati jīvayati dhārayati vardhayati adṛṣṭanimittena karmaṇā sa khalu āpyo raso yakṛtplīhādiṃ prāpya rāgam upaiti bhavanti vā atra ślokāḥ // 67
body.translated_text: And so it is said in the <s>Suśruta</s> (Saṃhitā): 'Here indeed, of food that is composed of the five elements, of four kinds, endowed with six tastes, having two kinds of taste-potency, having eight kinds of taste-potency, consumed in various ways and digested — that which is the fiery essence, subtle in form, that is called <s>rasa</s> (nutritive fluid). Its seat is the heart. From the heart it enters the twenty-four <s>dhamanīs</s> (vessels) — ten going upward, ten downward, and four going transversely — and day by day it nourishes, enlivens, sustains, and causes growth of the entire body, by the unseen cause of <s>karma</s> (action). That watery <s>rasa</s>, reaching the liver (<s>yakṛt</s>), spleen (<s>plīhā</s>), and so on, attains redness. And on this there are verses:' // 67

body.text: rañjitās tejasā tv āpaḥ śarīrasthena dehinām // 68
body.translated_text: The waters within the body of embodied beings, colored by the fire (of digestion), // 68

body.text: avyāpannāḥ prasannena raktam ity eva tad viduḥ // 69
body.translated_text: unimpaired and clear — that they know as blood (<s>rakta</s>). // 69

body.text: rasād eva striyo raktaṃ rajaḥsaṃjñaṃ pravartate // 70
body.translated_text: From <s>rasa</s> alone, in women, blood flows forth, designated as <s>rajas</s> (menstrual fluid). // 70

body.text: tadvaśād dvādaśād ūrdhvaṃ yāti pañcāśatiḥ kṣitim // 71
body.translated_text: From the twelfth (year) onward by its power, it ceases at the fiftieth year. // 71
The menstrual blood (<s>ārtava</s>) is fiery (<s>śoṇita</s>), because the embryo (<s>garbha</s>) is of the nature of both fire and moon (<s>agnīṣomīya</s>). // 72

body.text: rasād raktaṃ tato māṃsaṃ māṃsamedaś ca jāyate // 73
body.translated_text: From <s>rasa</s> comes blood (<s>rakta</s>), from that flesh (<s>māṃsa</s>), and from flesh, fat (<s>medas</s>) is produced; // 73
from fat comes bone (<s>asthi</s>), from that marrow (<s>majjā</s>), and from marrow, semen (<s>śukra</s>) arises. // 74

body.text: evaṃ māṃsena śukratvaṃ raso yāti yathākramam // 75
body.translated_text: Thus, through flesh, <s>rasa</s> gradually attains the state of semen (<s>śukra</s>). // 75
For women likewise, in a month the menstrual blood (<s>ārtava</s>) is produced. // 76
Thus. // 77

body.text: tad evaṃbhūte mātṛpitṛsambandhasambhūte agnīṣomātmake raktaretasī kusumasamayād anantaraṃ jananījaṭhare retaḥ kalilībhavati tato budbudam tataḥ peśī tato ghanaḥ yāvad aṅgaparigrahaḥ aṅgavyaktiḥ saṃvidullāsaḥ sarvāṅgasampattir ojaḥsaṃcāraḥ sukhaduḥkhasaṃvittir iti yāvat prajāyate // 78
body.translated_text: In this manner, born from the union of mother and father, being of the nature of fire and moon (<s>agnīṣomātmaka</s>), the blood and semen — immediately after the time of menstrual flowering, in the womb of the mother — the semen becomes a gelatinous mass (<s>kalila</s>), then a bubble (<s>budbuda</s>), then a lump of flesh (<s>peśī</s>), then a solid mass (<s>ghana</s>), until there is the formation of limbs, the manifestation of limbs, the arising of consciousness, the completion of all limbs, the circulation of vitality (<s>ojas</s>), the awareness of pleasure and pain — and thus until it is born. // 78
It is stated in the <s>Śrīcillācakreśvaramata</s>: 'From the mutual friction of the efflorescence of <s>Soma</s> (moon) and <s>Sūrya</s> (sun), // 79
when the fire (<s>Jātavedas</s>) is born, expanding in the middle channel, // 80
by the transformation of the heroic and ruddy (essences), the sprout arises.' // 81
'The semen deposited after one night enters the gelatinous state (<s>kalila</s>); // 82
it becomes a bubble (<s>budbuda</s>) in seven nights, and a lump of flesh (<s>peśī</s>) is produced in a month. // 83
In the second month it becomes solid (<s>ghana</s>); in the third, there is the taking hold by fire; // 84
in the fourth, consciousness arises in the limbs and their parts; // 85
in the sixth, the differentiation of all limbs; in the seventh, the arising of movement; // 86
in the eighth, vitality (<s>tejas</s>) circulates; in the ninth, sensation arises; // 87
in the tenth month, with body complete, the creature is born. // 88
Being born, touched by wind (<s>vāyu</s>), pressed by the mechanism of the birth-canal, // 89
it does not remember the fierce torment arising from many (previous) existences.' // 90
Gradually these causes of the body increase: // 91

body.text: rasaḥ sthitiṃ prakurute raktaṃ saṃjīvayaty alam // 92
body.translated_text: <s>rasa</s> (nutritive fluid) maintains stability; blood (<s>rakta</s>) fully enlivens; // 92

body.text: māṃsaṃ bṛṃhayati prāyo medaḥ snehayati sphuṭam // 93
body.translated_text: flesh (<s>māṃsa</s>) mostly causes nourishment; fat (<s>medas</s>) clearly provides lubrication; // 93
bones (<s>asthi</s>) support likewise, and marrow (<s>majjā</s>) is the inner essential substance; // 94
semen (<s>śukra</s>) produces joy and exaltation; urine (<s>mūtra</s>) separates moisture; // 95
feces (<s>purīṣa</s>) is declared to restrain wind (<s>vāyu</s>) and fire (<s>agni</s>); // 96
sweat provides moisture, and menstrual blood (<s>ārtava</s>) is the cause of conception. // 97
Having thus obtained this body with its six sheaths, through its possession, // 98

body.text: anapekṣya nijaṃ bhāvaṃ pumān bhāvān apekṣate // 99
body.translated_text: disregarding one's own true nature, a person attends to (worldly) objects.' // 99
Thus. // 100

body.text: ayam eva ca artho niruktikṛtāpi uktapārthivān aṣṭau guṇān vidyāt trīn mātṛtaḥ trīn pitṛtaḥ ityādy upakramya uktaḥ // 101
body.translated_text: This very meaning is also stated by the etymologist (<s>Niruktikṛt</s>), beginning with 'one should know eight earthly qualities — three from the mother, three from the father,' and so on. // 101

body.text: atraiva idaṃ puṃstrīnapuṃsakalakṣaṇaṃ prakṛtitrayakāraṇam somādhikyena puṃjanma sūryādhikyena yoṣitaḥ // 102
body.translated_text: Here also, regarding the characteristics of male, female, and neuter, and the cause of the three natures: 'By the predominance of <s>Soma</s> (moon), male birth; by the predominance of <s>Sūrya</s> (sun), female birth; // 102

body.text: sāmyāt klības tu vātena bhedāt syād bahvapatyatā // 103
body.translated_text: by their equality, a neuter (<s>klība</s>); and by wind (<s>vāta</s>) causing division, there is birth of many offspring.' // 103
Thus. // 104

body.text: avayavabhedo 'pi navame daśame māsi prabalaiḥ sūtimārutaiḥ // 105
body.translated_text: The differentiation of limbs also (occurs), and in the ninth or tenth month, by powerful birthing winds (<s>sūtimāruta</s>), // 105
the feverish (child) is expelled through the opening of the birth mechanism, like an arrow. // 106

body.text: tasya ṣoḍhā śarīraṃ tatṣaṭtvaco dhārayanti ca // 107
body.translated_text: Its body has six layers — six skins envelop it; // 107
and the bones are bound together, three hundred and sixty in number; // 108

body.text: sthūlaiḥ saha catuḥṣaṣṭir daśanā viṃśatir nakhāḥ // 109
body.translated_text: together with the large (bones), sixty-four; the teeth are twenty, the nails twenty; // 109
the rod-bones of the hands and feet, and their sockets are four sets; // 110

body.text: ṣaṣṭyaṅgulīnāṃ dve pārṣṇī gulpheṣu ca catuṣṭayam // 111
body.translated_text: sixty finger-bones, two heels, and in the ankles there are four; // 111

body.text: catvāry aratnikāsthīni jaṅghayos tāvad eva tu // 112
body.translated_text: four forearm-bones, and in the shanks just as many; // 112
two each in the knees, temples, thighs, and shoulder-joints; // 113
the eye-sockets and the hip-bones should also be specified; // 114

body.text: bhagāsthy ekaṃ tathā pṛṣṭhe catvāriṃśac ca pañca ca // 115
body.translated_text: one pelvic bone, and in the back forty-five; // 115

body.text: grīvā pañcadaśāsthīni jatrv ekaṃ ca tathā hanuḥ // 116
body.translated_text: the neck has fifteen bones, one collarbone, and likewise one jawbone; // 116
at its root two, and dense bones of the forehead, eyes, cheeks, and nose; // 117

body.text: parśukās talakaiḥ sārdham arbude ca dvisaptatiḥ // 118
body.translated_text: the ribs together with their cartilages, and the muscular masses, seventy-two; // 118

body.text: dvau śaṅkhakau kapālāni catvāry eva śiras tathā // 119
body.translated_text: two temple-bones, and four skull-plates in the head likewise; // 119
the chest has fifteen bones — this is the enumeration of bones in a person. // 120
Thus. // 121

Among these very (bones), the designations are stated in other treatises with distinctions such as skull-plate (<s>kapāla</s>), supporting-bone (<s>bharaṇa</s>), cartilage (<s>turuṇḍa</s>), vertebra (<s>ruṇḍa</s>), disc (<s>rucaka</s>), shaft (<s>nala</s>), rod (<s>yaṣṭī</s>), seed-bone (<s>lana</s>), and plate (<s>laka</s>). // 122

He states the other bodily sites: 'The muscle-fat (<s>vasā</s>), the omentum (<s>vapā</s>), the expulsive organ, the navel, the pancreas (<s>kloma</s>), the liver (<s>yakṛt</s>), the spleen (<s>plihā</s>); // 123
the small intestine (<s>kṣudrāntra</s>), the caecum (<s>vṛkśaka</s>), the bladder (<s>vasti</s>), and the rectum (<s>purīṣāpāna</s>) indeed; // 124

body.text: āmāśayo 'tha hṛdayaṃ sthūlāntraṃ gudam eva ca // 125
body.translated_text: the stomach (<s>āmāśaya</s>), and then the heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>), the large intestine (<s>sthūlāntra</s>), and the anus (<s>guda</s>) indeed; // 125

body.text: uttarau ca gudau koṣṭhau vistāro 'yam udāhṛtaḥ // 126
body.translated_text: and the two upper intestinal passages and the visceral cavities — this extent is described. // 126
The pupils (<s>kanīnike</s>), the bony ridges of the eyes (<s>ākṣikūṭe</s>), the conchae (<s>śaṣkulī</s>), the ear-cavities (<s>karṇaputrike</s>); // 127
the cheeks (<s>gaṇḍau</s>), the temples (<s>śaṅkhau</s>), the eyebrows (<s>bhruvau</s>), the eyelids (<s>kaṣṭaveṣṭau</s>), the lips (<s>oṣṭhau</s>), the hip-joints (<s>kukundare</s>); // 128
the groins (<s>vaṅkṣaṇau</s>), the testicles (<s>vṛṣaṇau</s>), the kidneys (<s>vṛkkau</s>), the phlegm-masses (<s>śleṣmasaṃghātikau</s>), the breasts (<s>stanau</s>); // 129
the epiglottis (<s>upajihvā</s>), the buttocks (<s>sphijau</s>), the tongue (<s>jihvā</s>), the shanks (<s>jaṅghe</s>), the thighs (<s>ūrū</s>), and the calves (<s>piṇḍike</s>); // 130
the palate (<s>tālu</s>), the abdomen (<s>udara</s>), the bladder (<s>vasti</s>), the crown of the head (<s>śīrṣa</s>), the chin (<s>cibuka</s>), the throat (<s>galaśuṇḍikā</s>); // 131
the four (sets of) eyelashes (<s>akṣipakṣma</s>), and the soles of the feet, palms of the hands, and the heart-region; // 132

body.text: avaṭuś caivam ādīni sthānāny atra śarīrake // 133
body.translated_text: the nape of the neck (<s>avaṭu</s>) and such others — these are the sites within this body. // 133
The nine openings — these are also the seats of the vital breath (<s>prāṇa</s>). // 134

body.text: dhamanīnāṃ śate dve tu pañcapeśīśatāni ca // 135
body.translated_text: Two hundred <s>dhamanīs</s> (vessels), and five hundred muscles (<s>peśīs</s>).' // 135
Thus. // 136

body.text: strīṇāṃ ca stanayor gartād aṣṭātriṃśadadhikāḥ sapeśyo dhamanyo bhavanti iti sauśrutaḥ // 137
body.translated_text: In women, from the cavity of the two breasts, there are thirty-eight additional muscles and vessels — so says the <s>Suśruta</s> (Saṃhitā). // 137
'Twenty-nine <s>lakṣas</s> (2,900,000) and nine hundred sinews (<s>snāyu</s>); // 138
fifty-six should be known as veins (<s>sirā</s>) in the network of vessels (<s>dhamanī</s>); // 139

body.text: saptottaraṃ marmaśataṃ dve tu saṃdhiśate tathā // 140
body.translated_text: one hundred and seven vital points (<s>marmas</s>), and two hundred joints (<s>sandhis</s>) likewise; // 140

body.text: lomnāṃ koṭyas tu pañcāśaccatasraḥ koṭya eva ca // 141
body.translated_text: fifty-four <s>koṭis</s> (540 million) of body hairs; // 141
nine handfuls (<s>añjali</s>) of <s>rasa</s> (nutritive fluid) should be known, and ten handfuls of water; // 142

body.text: sapta vai tu purīṣasya raktasyāṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ // 143
body.translated_text: seven (handfuls) of feces, and eight of blood are declared; // 143

body.text: śleṣmā ṣaṭ pañca pittaṃ ca catvāro mūtram eva ca // 144
body.translated_text: six of phlegm (<s>śleṣman</s>), five of bile (<s>pitta</s>), and four of urine; // 144

body.text: vasātrayaṃ ca dvau medo majjaikārdhaṃ ca mastake // 145
body.translated_text: three of fat (<s>vasā</s>), two of adipose tissue (<s>medas</s>), and one and a half of marrow (<s>majjā</s>) in the head; // 145

body.text: śleṣmaujasas tāvad eva retasas tāvad eva ca // 146
body.translated_text: the same amount of phlegmatic essence (<s>śleṣmaujas</s>), and the same amount of semen (<s>retas</s>). // 146

body.text: ity etad asthiraṃ varṣma yasya mokṣāya kṛty asau // 147
body.translated_text: This body is thus impermanent — one whose task is its liberation (should strive for <s>mokṣa</s>).' // 147
Thus (is the description) of a healthy body with balanced constitution. // 148

body.text: anyathā tu vailakṣaṇyāc charīrāṇām asvasthatvāt tathaiva ca // 149
body.translated_text: But otherwise, due to the variation of bodies and their unhealthy states, // 149
no fixed measure of the <s>doṣas</s> (humors), <s>dhātus</s> (tissues), and <s>malas</s> (wastes) exists. // 150
So it is stated. // 151

body.text: tad etat vibhāgena bībhatsadarśanaṃ vairāgyamunibhir agāyi tathā cāhuḥ asthisthūṇaṃ snāyuyutaṃ māṃsaśoṇitalepanam // 152
body.translated_text: This (body), analyzed in its parts, is disgusting to behold; it was praised by the sages of dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>). And so they say: 'A pillar of bones, bound with sinews, plastered with flesh and blood, // 152
covered with skin, foul-smelling, filled with urine and feces; // 153
afflicted by old age and sorrow, the abode of disease, tormented, // 154

body.text: rajasvalam anityaṃ ca bhūtāvāsam imaṃ tyajet muniḥ pārāśaryo 'pi āha sarvāśucinidhānasya kṛtaghnasya vināśinaḥ // 155
body.translated_text: stained with passion, impermanent — this dwelling of beings should be abandoned.' The sage <s>Pārāśarya</s> (<s>Vyāsa</s>) also said: 'For this body that is a storehouse of all impurity, ungrateful, perishable — // 155
for the sake of this body alone, fools commit sins. // 156
For that which is sustained by food, gradually, with difficulty, finding pleasure — // 157

body.text: ko hi nāma śarīrāya dharmāpetaṃ samācaret // 158
body.translated_text: who indeed would act contrary to <s>Dharma</s> for the sake of (such a) body?' // 158
Thus. // 159

body.text: evaṃ śarīram uktvā śarīrisvarūpam ucyate dvāsaptatisahasrāṇi hṛdayād abhiniḥsṛtāḥ // 160
body.translated_text: Having thus described the body, the nature of the embodied soul is now stated: 'Seventy-two thousand (channels) issuing forth from the heart, // 160

body.text: hitā nāmāhitā nāḍyas tāsāṃ madhye śaśiprabham // 161
body.translated_text: called <s>Hitā</s> and <s>Ahitā</s>, (are these) <s>nāḍīs</s> (subtle channels); in the midst of them, radiant like the moon, // 161

body.text: maṇḍalaṃ tasya madhyastha ātmā dīpa ivācalaḥ // 162
body.translated_text: is a circle (<s>maṇḍala</s>), and stationed in its center is the <s>Ātman</s> (Self), like a steady lamp. // 162

body.text: sa jñeyas taṃ viditveha punar ājāyate na tu // 163
body.translated_text: That (Self) should be known; having known it here, one is not born again.' // 163

body.text: idam atra tātparyaṃ taṃ tathābhūtam ātmānaṃ viditvā naro na janmakleśam anubhavati kiṃbhūtaṃ yad dhṛdayoktaṃ dvāsaptatisaṃkhyāvacchinnaṃ nāḍīcakraṃ tad antar yat śaśimaṇḍalaṃ tadantaḥsthaṃ tāś ca nāḍyo 'śitapītarasasaṃcaraṇādhikāratvāt puṇyopacayena hitāḥ tadabhāvena ahitāḥ tāsāṃ saṃcāraka eka eva vyavahārabhedāt pañcabhedo vāyuḥ tāsāṃ ca dve pradhāne dakṣiṇottarasambaddhe agnīṣomātmake taddvāreṇa prāṇasya ūrdhvagamanam ahaḥ adho 'pānasya rātriḥ etena ardhamāsamāsartuvatsarādikālavibhāgo 'pi vyākhyātaḥ samaprāṇacāro viṣuvat tayor madhye tṛtīyā daṇḍākārā brahmanāḍī sthitā tatra niruddhaprāṇo yogī dīpākāram ātmānaṃ paśyati iti ata evoktaṃ samyagdarśanasampannaḥ karmabhir na sa badhyate // 164
body.translated_text: The purport here is this: having known the self as it truly is, a person does not experience the suffering of birth. What is that [self]? The <s>nāḍīcakra</s> (circle of channels), delimited by the number seventy-two, as stated in the heart [teaching] — within it is the lunar disc; stationed within that are those <s>nāḍīs</s>. Since they are responsible for the circulation of the essence of what is eaten and drunk, they are beneficial through the accumulation of merit, and harmful in its absence. The one that causes their circulation is a single <s>vāyu</s> (wind), which becomes fivefold due to differences in function. Of those, two are primary, connected to the right and left, having the nature of fire and moon. Through those two, the upward movement of <s>prāṇa</s> is daytime; the downward movement of <s>apāna</s> is nighttime. By this, the division of time into half-months, months, seasons, years, and so forth is also explained. The equal movement of <s>prāṇa</s> is the equinox. Between those two stands the third, the staff-shaped <s>brahmanāḍī</s>. The <s>yogin</s> who has restrained <s>prāṇa</s> therein sees the self in the form of a lamp-flame. Hence it is said: 'One endowed with right vision is not bound by <s>karmas</s> (actions).'
One deprived of [right] vision enters into <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence).
Thus.

body.text: saṃsārapravṛttau ca tasya kalāto viṣayavibhedo munibhir uktaḥ tathā hi paradravyāṇy abhidhyāyaṃs tathāniṣṭāni cintayan // 167
body.translated_text: And regarding the continuance of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the sages have taught the differentiation of objects through his <s>kalās</s> (phases). Thus: 'Coveting the possessions of others, and thinking about undesirable things,'
'And being attached to falsehood — one is born in the lowest wombs.'
'A person who speaks falsely, and likewise a person who slanders,'
'And one who babbles incoherently — is born among animals and birds.'
'One delighting in taking what is not given, one who serves another's wife,'
'And one who harms without proper conduct — is born among immovable beings.'

body.text: ityādi ayaṃ tu uktayātanasya niyogaḥ advayarūpasya ātmanaḥ kutastyo 'yaṃ bhedaḥ iti cet māyāmahāmohavikalpakalpita ity āha ākāśam ekaṃ hi yathā ghaṭādiṣu pṛthag bhavet // 173
body.translated_text: And so forth. But this is the assignment of the stated destinations. If the self is of non-dual nature, whence comes this differentiation? [In reply:] It is imagined through the conceptual constructions of <s>māyā</s> (illusion) and great delusion. Thus it is said: 'Just as one space becomes differentiated in pots and the like,'
'So too the one self appears as many, like the sun in bodies of water.'
Thus.

body.text: na ca apakvakaṣāyasya kadācid api uktarūpam ātmajñānaṃ bhavati tathā ca malino hi yathādarśo rūpālokasya na kṣamaḥ // 176
body.translated_text: And for one whose impurities are not matured, self-knowledge of the stated nature never arises. And thus: 'Just as a dirty mirror is not capable of [reflecting] form and light,'

body.text: tathā hy apakvakaraṇa ātmajñānasya na kṣamaḥ // 177
body.translated_text: 'So too one of unmatured faculties is not capable of self-knowledge.'
And so forth has been stated.
Enough of further elaboration.

body.text: evam asau bhagavān svātantryaśaktimahimnā paśudaśām avalambamāno bhogopadānapravaṇaḥ sampūrṇadehaprāṇabalaḥ san uktena ṣaḍadhvajālakrameṇa prabuddhaḥ śarīraparigraham āsādayati krameṇa bhukteṣu karmasu ṣaḍbhir bhāvavikārair jarārogādibhiḥ kāyayantre vighaṭamāne dehastambho vepathur nāḍīcakrasaṃkocaḥ kvacid viparyayeṇa tadvikāso marmabhaṅgaḥ śoṣa ityādi pūrvasaṃsthāpanopamardakaṃ sarvam upapadyate yāvat vinaśyati vināśaś ca kṣaṇiko 'sya yady api tathāpi sthūlayā vṛttyā daśabhir daśabhir abhivyaktaḥ proktaḥ // 180
body.translated_text: Thus that <s>Bhagavān</s> (Lord), by the majesty of his power of autonomy, assuming the condition of a bound soul, inclined toward the enjoyment of experience, possessing full bodily strength and <s>prāṇa</s>, having been awakened through the stated sequence of the net of six courses, obtains embodiment. Gradually, as <s>karmas</s> are experienced, through six modifications of existence — old age, disease, and the rest — as the bodily mechanism deteriorates, the pillar of the body trembles, the <s>nāḍīcakra</s> contracts, or conversely expands, the vital points break down, desiccation occurs, and so forth — everything that undermines the previous constitution takes place, until [the body] perishes. And although its destruction is momentary, nevertheless, in a gross manner, it has been described as manifest in periods of ten by ten [years].

body.text: tathā hi bālyaṃ vṛddhir balaṃ prajñā tvak cakṣuḥ śrotram indriyam // 181
body.translated_text: Thus: 'Childhood, growth, strength, intelligence, skin, sight, hearing, faculty,'

body.text: āsanaṃ śayanaṃ puṃsāṃ daśabhir daśabhir vrajet // 182
body.translated_text: 'Sitting capacity, and lying capacity — these proceed by tens for human beings.'
Thus it has been stated.

body.text: tataś ca tasmin śarīrayantre vighaṭite sā saṃvit prāṇanātmatām avalambya ātivāhikena dehena dehāntaraṃ nīyate tataś ca ātivāhikaṃ śarīrakaṃ bhūtabhaviṣyaddehāntarāle yugyasthānīyaṃ sambhavati yadārūḍho 'sau pudgalaḥ śarīrāntarāsaṅgam anubhavati uktaṃ ca kośabhāṣye mṛtyūpapattibhavayor antarā bhavatīha yaḥ // 184
body.translated_text: Then, when that bodily mechanism has broken down, that consciousness, assuming the nature of the life-force, is carried by means of the <s>ātivāhika</s> (transmigrating) body to another body. And that <s>ātivāhika</s> body arises in the interval between the past and future bodies, serving as a yoke-like vehicle, mounted upon which that individual experiences the connection to another body. As stated in the <s>Kośabhāṣya</s> (Abhidharmakośabhāṣya): 'That which exists here between the states of death and rebirth,'
'Is called the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>), because of its connection with the destination to be reached.'
'Like the continuity of a rice plant, its arising is uninterrupted.'
'[The analogy of] a reflection does not hold, because it is not established, and because the example is dissimilar.'
'It [the intermediate being] exists after the moment of death and before [the moment of] rebirth.'
'It perceives [only] the pure <s>karma</s> of its own class, and discerns the <s>karma</s> visible to the sense faculties.'
Thus.

body.text: śrutiś ca dve te cakre sūrye brahmāṇa ṛtuthā viduḥ // 191
body.translated_text: And the <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture) [says]: 'Two wheels of the sun, the <s>brahmāṇas</s> (knowers of <s>Brahman</s>) know them according to the seasons.'

body.text: athaikaṃ cakraṃ yad guhā tad addhātaya id viduḥ // 192
body.translated_text: 'But the one wheel that is hidden — that the knowers of the path know.'

body.text: iti ayam arthaḥ he sūrye bhagavati ātmaśakte brahmāṇaḥ brahmavādinaḥ ṛtuthā kāle kāle te tava sambandhinī dve cakre viduḥ cakram iva cakraṃ parivartasādharmyāt śarīram ucyate tayor dvitvaṃ vartamānabhāvibhedāt atas tayor antare kathitayā yuktyā yad ekam ātivāhikākhyaṃ tat guhā guptam anupalakṣyam ity arthaḥ ata eva tad addhātayaḥ it viduḥ yogina eva jānanti iti tātparyam // 193
body.translated_text: The meaning is this: O sun, O <s>Bhagavatī</s> (divine power of the self), the <s>brahmāṇas</s>, the expounders of <s>Brahman</s>, know your two wheels at the proper times — the body is called a wheel because of its similarity to a wheel in revolving. Their duality is due to the distinction between present and future [bodies]. Therefore, that one [wheel] in between those two, called the <s>ātivāhika</s>, known by the reasoning stated, is hidden — meaning concealed and imperceptible. Hence 'the knowers of the path know it' — the purport is that only <s>yogins</s> know it.

body.text: tathā ca jāgradavasthāyāṃ dṛḍhakaraṇasya pramātur indriyāṇi śrotrādīni śabdādayaś ca viṣayā bhavanti tathā prameyasamaye pracalitam antaḥkaraṇam indriyaṃ yiyāsutā ca viṣayaḥ tām eva yiyāsutām adhikṛtya pravaramuniḥ pārāśaryaḥ samādhitavān yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaran bhāvaṃ tyajaty ante kalevaram // 194
body.translated_text: And thus: in the waking state, the sense faculties — hearing and the rest — and their objects — sound and the rest — belong to the cognizer whose faculties are firm. Likewise, at the time of death, the inner organ that has become agitated is the faculty, and the desire to depart is the object. Addressing precisely that desire to depart, the supreme sage <s>Pārāśarya</s> (<s>Vyāsa</s>) has established: 'Whatever state of being one remembers when abandoning the body at the end,'

body.text: taṃ tam evaiti kaunteya sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ // 195
body.translated_text: 'That very state one attains, O <s>Kaunteya</s> (son of <s>Kuntī</s>), being always absorbed in that state of mind.'
Thus.

body.text: ayam atra saṃkṣepārthaḥ sambhavabhogaḥ janmabhogaḥ sthitibhogaś ca iti tisraḥ śarīrasya prāgavasthā bhavanti hi tathā hi jaṭhare cetanāyāṃ saṃjātāyāṃ garbhabhogaḥ prasavasamaye janmabhogaḥ prasūtasya bālyādivayaḥparāvṛttyā vicitraḥ sthitibhogaḥ // 197
body.translated_text: Here is the summary meaning: the experience of conception, the experience of birth, and the experience of continuance — these are the three prior states of the body. Thus: when consciousness arises in the womb, there is the experience of the womb; at the time of delivery, there is the experience of birth; and for the one who is born, through the progression of ages beginning with childhood, there is the varied experience of continuance.

body.text: mṛtibhogaḥ yiyāsutā ca dve caramāvasthe tatra mṛtibhogaḥ vicitrā śarīrapīḍā yiyāsutā ātivāhikaśarīrasambaddhā tām eva ca yiyāsutām uddiśya yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaran bhāvam // 198
body.translated_text: The experience of death and the desire to depart are the two final states. Of these, the experience of death is the various bodily afflictions; the desire to depart is connected with the <s>ātivāhika</s> (transmigrating) body. And addressing precisely that desire to depart, 'Whatever state of being one remembers' —

body.text: ityādi pravṛttam ata eva bhūtabhaviṣyadarthahitārthavādinaḥ smarann iti śabdapratyayasya yathārthaḥ prayogaḥ syāt etad eva ca vitatya śrītantrāloke pratipāditam mṛtibhogaḥ samasto 'yaṃ marmacchin mūḍhatākṣagaḥ // 199
body.translated_text: And so forth has been set forth. Therefore, for one who speaks of what is beneficial regarding past and future purposes, the word 'remembering' (<s>smaran</s>) is used in its proper sense. This very matter has been extensively established in the <s>Śrī Tantrāloka</s>: 'This entire experience of death involves the breaking of vital points and the condition of confused faculties.'
'Therein there is the bewilderment of the faculties, and the state of being overcome by labored breathing.'

body.text: yas tv asau kṣaṇa evaikaś caramaḥ prāṇanātmakaḥ // 201
body.translated_text: 'But that single final moment, which is of the nature of the life-force,'
'That is the time-portion of leaving the body, the separation from <s>prāṇa</s>.'
'At that [moment], whatever one remembers, through the awakening of prior impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>),'
'That very form one assumes, deluded by pleasure and pain.'
Thus.

body.text: atra ca viṣayanaiyatyena vibhāgo vyāsamuninaiva kṛtaḥ // 206
body.translated_text: And here, the differentiation according to the specific objects [remembered] has been made by the sage <s>Vyāsa</s> himself:

body.text: yadā sattve vivṛddhe tu pralayaṃ yāti dehabhṛt // 207
body.translated_text: 'When <s>sattva</s> has increased, the embodied one goes to dissolution' —
And so forth, by that text.

body.text: tā etāḥ śarīrāvasthāḥ pañcāre cakre parivartamāne tasminn ātasthur bhuvanāni viśvā // 209
body.translated_text: These states of the body [are described] in [the <s>śruti</s>]: 'In the five-spoked wheel as it revolves, all beings are stationed' —
And so forth, as stated in the <s>śruti</s>.

body.text: anyatrāpi sambhavo janma sattā ca mṛtiś cātha yiyāsutā // 211
body.translated_text: Elsewhere too: 'Conception, birth, existence, death, and the desire to depart —'
'These are the five misfortunes of transformation for the body.'
Thus it has been stated.

body.text: etad evam uktarūpeṇa asau ātivāhikena dehena dehāntaraṃ nīyate so 'pi dehaḥ suptotthitāt prabodham avāpya prāṇiti uktena cakreṇa so 'pi vinaśyati yāvat araghaṭṭaghaṭīyantravat parivartamāno 'ṇuḥ nānākāyanikāyaiḥ saṃsarati saṃsāre // 214
body.translated_text: This being so, in the manner described, [the soul] is carried by the <s>ātivāhika</s> body to another body. That body too, having obtained awakening like one risen from sleep, lives; through the stated cycle, it too perishes. Thus, revolving like the buckets of a water-wheel, the atomic [soul] transmigrates through <s>saṃsāra</s> with various classes of bodies.

body.text: tathā ca śrutiḥ sasyam iva martyaḥ pacyate sasyam iva jāyate punaḥ // 215
body.translated_text: And the <s>śruti</s> [says]: 'Like grain the mortal ripens; like grain he is born again.'
Thus.
'Just as one discards worn-out garments' —
And so forth, this too has been stated by the sage <s>Vyāsa</s>.

body.text: atha kadācit parameśvarānugrahaśaktipātapavitritaḥ kenāpi dīkṣādinā upāyena saṃvidānandaviśrāntam advayaṃ nijaṃ rūpaṃ parāmṛśati tataḥ svarūpam ālambate yathoktaṃ śrīmālinīvijaye evam asyātmanaḥ kāle kasmiṃścid yogyatāvaśāt // 219
body.translated_text: But at some time, purified by the descent of the grace-power of the Supreme Lord, through some means such as <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), one grasps one's own non-dual nature, which rests in the bliss of consciousness. Then one abides in one's own true nature. As stated in the <s>Śrī Mālinīvijaya</s>: 'Thus, for this self, at some time, by force of fitness,'

body.text: ity upakramya tatkṣaṇād vopabhogād vā dehapāte śivaṃ vrajet // 220
body.translated_text: Beginning thus — 'From that very moment, or from the enjoyment [of initiation], or at the fall of the body, one goes to <s>Śiva</s>.'
Thus, by this concluding text.

body.text: yad vā kvāpi parameśvarāyatane śarīram ativāhya pūrve vidhau krameṇa parameśvarībhavati tad uktaṃ śrīsāttvatāyām prāsādadvāradeśāc ca yatra śaṅkhadhvaniś caran // 222
body.translated_text: Or else, having carried the body to some temple of the Supreme Lord, through the prior method, one gradually becomes one with the Supreme Lord. That has been stated in the <s>Śrī Sāttvata</s> [Saṃhitā]: 'From the vicinity of the temple door, where the sound of the conch travels,'

body.text: prayāti sarvato dikṣu tat kṣetraṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ matam // 223
body.translated_text: 'Going forth in all directions — that field is considered <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>.'
'That [merit] is proclaimed as double what is ordained by the sage.'

body.text: siddhāvatāritād devāt tad eva triguṇaṃ smṛtam // 225
body.translated_text: 'From a deity installed by a <s>Siddha</s>, that is remembered as triple.'
fourfold from the self-manifest, for those who have cultivated the self at the time of death. [226]

body.text: phalaṃ sāyujyatāpūrvaṃ vijñeyaṃ tu kramāt tataḥ // 227
body.translated_text: The fruit, beginning with <s>sāyujya</s> (union), should be known successively thereafter. [227]
The mind of humans, which is driven by impurity due to corrupted senses, [228]
that, at the time of death, attains purification in the abode of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. [229]
Thus. [230]

body.text: śrīmadamṛteśaśikhāyām api ye tu tattvāvatīrṇānāṃ śaṃkarājñānuvartinām // 231
body.translated_text: In the Śrīmad-<s>Amṛteśa-śikhā</s> also: Those who have descended into the truth, who follow the command of <s>Śaṅkara</s>— [231]
in the houses of <s>Svayambhū</s>, sages, divine seers, and human beings, [232]

body.text: mṛtās te tatpuraṃ prāpya pureśair dīkṣitāḥ kramāt // 233
body.translated_text: having died, they reach that city and are gradually initiated by the lords of that city. [233]

body.text: martye 'vatīrya vā nāvā prayānti paramaṃ padam // 234
body.translated_text: Or, descending to the mortal world by vessel, they proceed to the supreme state. [234]
Among those, the <s>Svayambhūs</s> are of two kinds: some are devoted to bestowing grace, [235]
some have come for their own purpose; the former are bestowers of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation). [236]
Thus. [237]

body.text: tatrāpi na sarvasya mokṣa ity uktam paśumātrasya sālokyaṃ sāmīpyaṃ dīkṣitasya tu // 238
body.translated_text: Even there, not everyone attains liberation, as it is stated: For the mere <s>paśu</s> (bound soul), <s>sālokya</s> (residence in the same world); for the initiated, <s>sāmīpya</s> (proximity). [238]

body.text: tatparasya tu sāyujyam ity ājñā pārameśvarī // 239
body.translated_text: For one devoted to that, <s>sāyujya</s> (union)—this is the supreme command of the Lord. [239]

body.text: yas tūrdhvaśāstragas tatra tyaktāsthaḥ saṃśayena saḥ // 240
body.translated_text: But one who, though versed in the higher scripture, has abandoned it through doubt— [240]

body.text: vrajed āyatanaṃ naiva sa phalaṃ kiṃcid aśnute // 241
body.translated_text: he does not reach the <s>āyatana</s> (abode) and obtains no fruit whatsoever. [241]
Those who with their mind hate the knowledge of <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) and the <s>āyatana</s>, [242]

body.text: ācaranti ca tat te vai sarve nirayagāminaḥ // 243
body.translated_text: yet practice it—they indeed all go to hell. [243]

body.text: ye ca svabhyastavijñānamayāḥ śivamayā hi te // 244
body.translated_text: But those who are permeated with self-cultivated knowledge, who are filled with <s>Śiva</s>— [244]

body.text: jīvanmuktā na teṣāṃ syān mṛtau kāpi vicāraṇā // 245
body.translated_text: they are <s>jīvanmukta</s> (liberated while living); for them there is no deliberation at the time of death. [245]
Thus. [246]

body.text: ata eva uktaṃ śrīniśāṭane godoham iṣupātaṃ vā nayanonmīlanaṃ ca vā // 247
body.translated_text: Therefore it is said in the Śrī-<s>Niśāṭana</s>: The duration of milking a cow, the flight of an arrow, or the blinking of an eye— [247]

body.text: samyagyuktaḥ pare tattve na bhūyo janmabhāg bhavet // 248
body.translated_text: one properly united with the supreme truth is not born again. [248]

body.text: yasmāt pūrvaṃ pare nyasto yenātmā brahmaṇi svayam // 249
body.translated_text: Since one who has previously deposited the self in <s>Brahman</s> by one's own accord, [249]

body.text: smaraṇaṃ tu kathaṃ tasya prāṇānte samupasthite // 250
body.translated_text: how then can remembrance occur for such a one when the end of life has arrived? [250]
Thus. [251]

body.text: śrīrāmabhaṭṭārake 'pi tāvat kṣetraṃ tathā tīrthaṃ yāvad brahmaṇi no viśet // 252
body.translated_text: In the Śrī-<s>Rāmabhaṭṭāraka</s> also: As long as one has not entered into <s>Brahman</s>, so long are sacred fields and pilgrimage sites relevant. [252]

body.text: tad viditvā śvapāko 'pi matsamo nātra saṃśayaḥ // 253
body.translated_text: Having known that, even a <s>śvapāka</s> (outcaste) is equal to me—there is no doubt in this. [253]
Thus. [254]

body.text: bhagavatā bhegipatināpi tīrthe śvapacagṛhe vā naṣṭasmṛtir api parityajan deham // 255
body.translated_text: By the Blessed <s>Bhegipati</s> also: At a pilgrimage site or in the house of an outcaste, even one who has lost memory, abandoning the body— [255]
is liberated simultaneously with knowledge and goes to <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute freedom), free from sorrow. [256]
Thus. [257]

body.text: śrīmatpauṣkarāyām api uktam kṣityantānāṃ ca tattvānāṃ devatvena vyavasthitaḥ // 258
body.translated_text: In the Śrīmat-<s>Pauṣkara</s> also it is stated: One who is established as divine among the <s>tattvas</s> (principles) ending with earth, [258]
a knower of <s>mantras</s>, devoted to the Lord, faithful, and ever believing, [259]
wherever, in whatever <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life), he may dwell with senses controlled, [260]
always remembering the <s>mantra</s> placed within his own body, with form surrendered, [261]
at the time of abandoning the body, resting wherever he may be, [262]

body.text: prayāti padam ādyaṃ vai samutkrāntaḥ svavigraham // 263
body.translated_text: he goes to the primordial state, having departed from his own body. [263]
Thus. [264]

body.text: anyatrāpi śarīram evāyatanaṃ nānyad āyatanaṃ vrajet // 265
body.translated_text: Elsewhere also: The body itself is the <s>āyatana</s> (temple); one should not seek another abode. [265]

body.text: tīrtham ekaṃ śrayen mantram anyatīrthāni varjayet iti // 266
body.translated_text: One should resort to the single pilgrimage of the <s>mantra</s> and abandon other pilgrimages. [266]

body.text: tathā svasthaceṣṭāś ca ye martyāḥ smaranti mama nārada // 267
body.translated_text: Likewise: Those mortals who, while healthy and active, remember me, O <s>Nārada</s>, [267]
those, even if like wood or stone at the time of death, I remember. [268]
Thus it is said. [269]

body.text: na ca saṃsthitasya uttamatayā adhikāriṇo lokayātrāprasiddhāsruvimocanādiparidevitaṃ kāryam yathoktaṃ śrīpūrvaśāsane niṣiddhaṃ sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ rodanaṃ kāyaśāsanam // 270
body.translated_text: And for one who has passed away as a supreme qualified practitioner, there should be no worldly lamentation such as the shedding of tears, as stated in the Śrī-<s>Pūrvaśāsana</s>: Weeping is forbidden by all scriptures; it is the discipline of the body. [270]
Especially in the <s>Bhairava Tantra</s>, it is considered a rite of the bound. [271]

body.text: ayuktam imam ācāraṃ tyajed vai naurdhvadaihikam // 272
body.translated_text: This improper practice should be abandoned, especially the post-mortem rites. [272]
Thus. [273]

body.text: śrīmatarahasyatilake 'pi uttamanayādhikāriṇāṃ saṃvṛtanijasadācārāṇāṃ lokaprasiddhirakṣāyai tadācārāparityāgo 'pi āmnātaḥ tathā hi lokācārasya vicchedo na kartavyaḥ kadācana // 274
body.translated_text: In the Śrīmat-<s>Rahasyatilaka</s> also, for those qualified practitioners of the highest path who have concealed their true conduct, the non-abandonment of worldly practices is also enjoined for the protection of public propriety. As it says: The practice of the world should never be interrupted. [274]

body.text: guhyaṃ guhyataraṃ kāryaṃ bāhyaṃ bāhyāntaraṃ tathā iti // 275
body.translated_text: What is secret should be kept most secret; what is external should remain outwardly so. [275]

body.text: anayoś ca pakṣayor ekatarapakṣāvalambane pravaragurava eva pramāṇam // 276
body.translated_text: And in adhering to either of these two positions, the most excellent <s>gurus</s> alone are the authority. [276]

body.text: pitruddeśena ca yāgajapahomopavāsādi gurum ārādhya avaśyaṃ vidhātavyam ity uktam śrīmahākule āsūtrite bhāgalupte yatheṣṭarajasānvite // 277
body.translated_text: For the sake of the departed ancestors, <s>yāga</s> (sacrifice), <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>homa</s> (fire offering), fasting, and the like must necessarily be performed after propitiating the <s>guru</s>, as stated in the Śrīmat-<s>Mahākula</s>: In a maṇḍala prescribed by ritual, even when the thread is torn, the portion lost, and stained with impurity as it may be, [277]
even without invoking the <s>mantra</s>, [278]
seven <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>mantras</s> establish their presence. [279]
How much more so when the <s>Kaulika</s> tradition, having been invoked there, is duly worshipped! [280]
Dedicating it to the ancestors, O blessed one, it leads to their infinite merit. [281]
Thus. [282]

body.text: śrīpracaṇḍabhairave 'pi uktam tanuvittāś ca ye martyā gurumantraparāyaṇāḥ // 283
body.translated_text: In the Śrī-<s>Pracaṇḍabhairava</s> also it is stated: Those mortals who are of meager wealth but devoted to the <s>guru</s>'s <s>mantra</s>, [283]
who are especially unable to perform the great sacrifice and worship, [284]

body.text: siddhaliṅgaṃ tadā teṣāṃ pitrarthaṃ pūjayed budhaḥ // 285
body.translated_text: for them, a wise person should worship the <s>siddha-liṅga</s> for the sake of their ancestors. [285]

body.text: ucitaṃ pūjanaṃ tatra devānām api durlabham // 286
body.translated_text: The worship performed there is rare even for the gods. [286]

body.text: kulāny uddharate tatra daśa pūrvāparāṇy api // 287
body.translated_text: It uplifts ten generations, both past and future. [287]
Thus. [288]
In the Śrī-<s>Bhāgeśa</s> tradition also: By poison, serpents, fire, epilepsy, hunger, excessive eating, imprisonment, [289]
by outcastes, floods, storms, royal punishment, and thieves, [290]
by the heat of summer, cold, wagons, spiders, exposure, and great calamities, [291]
by brahmins, barbarians, heretics, by the <s>Nirmūla</s> and <s>Uḍḍāmara</s> methods, [292]

body.text: ye hatāḥ pāpakarmāṇo mitradroharatāś ca ye // 293
body.translated_text: those who are slain while performing sinful deeds, and those devoted to treachery against friends, [293]
and others who have committed treachery against their master, and likewise those who have destroyed themselves, [294]

body.text: gurviṇyo duścaritrāś ca prasavena hatāś ca yāḥ // 295
body.translated_text: and pregnant women, those of evil conduct, and those who die in childbirth— [295]
for them there is no other means of upliftment, O lady of excellent complexion, [296]

body.text: vinā yāgaṃ vinā homaṃ vinā mūrtiparigraham // 297
body.translated_text: without sacrifice, without <s>homa</s>, without the installation of an image, [297]
without a person brought through the practice of the great <s>Jāla</s> ritual— [298]
the <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) called 'upliftment of the dead,' which operates across all paths. [299]
This, then, is the procedure for those who follow the higher teaching. [300]

body.text: itareṣāṃ tu svaśāstrasamayopanyastānuṣṭhānam eva śreyaḥ tad alam anena // 301
body.translated_text: For others, the practice as prescribed by the conventions of their own scriptures is best. Enough of this. [301]

body.text: evaṃ samanantarodīritayā nītyā janmamaraṇaprabandhasambandham avadhārya akṛtrimasvarūpaparāmarśanena jīvanmuktim āsādya kṛtakṛtyatām ālambante santaḥ // 302
body.translated_text: Thus, having ascertained the connection of the continuum of birth and death according to the principle just expounded, the wise ones attain <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living) through the apprehension of their unconditioned true nature, and they reach the state of having accomplished all that is to be accomplished. [302]
As it is said: Those who know the truth of consciousness, from the ocean of awareness, having drunk [303]

body.text: amṛtam iti nigīrṇe kālakūṭe 'pi devā yadi pibata tadānīṃ niścitaṃ vaḥ śivatvam // 304
body.translated_text: the <s>amṛta</s> (nectar)—the extract pressed from the unwavering vigor of the heart—even when the <s>kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison) has been swallowed, O gods, if you drink it, then certainly you attain <s>Śivatva</s> (the state of <s>Śiva</s>). [304]
Thus. [305]
Having attained his position through the grace of the glorious master <s>Yogeśvarācārya</s>, [306]
<s>Vāmadeva</s> composed this inquiry into birth and death. [307]

body.text: abhinavamadamantharā puraṃdhrī madhusamaye madhurāś ca gītibandhāḥ // 308
body.translated_text: A young woman languid with fresh intoxication in the season of spring, and sweet song-compositions, [308]

body.text: bata bata hṛdayaṃ haranti vāco lalitapadāś ca rahasyavastugarbhāḥ // 309
body.translated_text: Alas, alas! Words steal the heart—those with graceful phrasing and pregnant with esoteric meaning. [309]
This is the work of the venerable great <s>Māheśvara</s> teacher, the excellent Śrīmad Bhaṭṭa <s>Vāmadeva</s>. [310]
When the array of scholars versed in sacred learning has diminished with the passage of time, [311]
by one intent solely on illuminating each and every true teaching, endowed with the energy of right discernment, for the sake of practical activity, [312]

body.text: śrīmatkaśmīrādhirājena mukhyair dharmodyuktair mantribhiḥ svair vivecya // 313
body.translated_text: the illustrious supreme king of <s>Kaśmīra</s>, having deliberated with his chief ministers devoted to <s>Dharma</s>, [313]
established an institution whose chief purpose is the recovery of texts pregnant with knowledge and wisdom. [314]
There, by the good people serving under the directorship of <s>Mukundarāma</s>, devoted for life, [315]

body.text: pūrtyā śuddhyā vyākhyayā saṃskṛtaḥ stāt pūrṇo granthaḥ śreyase sajjanānām // 316
body.translated_text: may this complete text be perfected through completion, purification, and commentary, for the welfare of the virtuous. [316]
<s>Tilaka</s> (ornamental verse). [317]
May this be an offering to <s>Śaṅkara</s> whose body is the nectar of self-consciousness! [318]
